unread.said: You walk west toward the vegetation, and the mist comes down over it thicker with every step, until you cannot see the ground you are walking on and have to turn back to find it.
unread.line: You walk west toward the vegetation, and the mist comes down over it thicker with every step, until you cannot see the ground you are walking on and have to turn back to find it.

unread.said: The path north along the beach runs between the surf and the rocks a little way, and is cut by a fall from the cliff above that the sea has made its own; you would have to swim the gap, and you have seen the surf. Not today.
unread.line: The path north along the beach runs between the surf and the rocks a little way, and is cut by a fall from the cliff above that the sea has made its own; you would have to swim the gap, and you have seen the surf. Not today.

unread.said: You climb over the rubble of the wall, and on the other side the mist is down so thick over the cliff-top that you cannot tell the ground from the drop, and you come back over the wall rather than find out which was which. You can hear quiet footsteps nearby.
unread.line: You climb over the rubble of the wall, and on the other side the mist is down so thick over the cliff-top that you cannot tell the ground from the drop, and you come back over the wall rather than find out which was which.

unread.said: A stone wall blocks the way.
unread.line: A stone wall blocks the way.

unread.said: The cramped way east runs a few yards and is choked with rock that came down from the roof some time ago; you get your light into the gap, and your arm, and no further. It will not be cleared today.
unread.line: The cramped way east runs a few yards and is choked with rock that came down from the roof some time ago; you get your light into the gap, and your arm, and no further. It will not be cleared today.

unread.said: The passage east narrows to a squeeze, and then to less than a squeeze: you get an arm in, and a shoulder, and stick, and come out again backwards with grit in your hair. It will take a thinner day than this one.
unread.line: The passage east narrows to a squeeze, and then to less than a squeeze: you get an arm in, and a shoulder, and stick, and come out again backwards with grit in your hair. It will take a thinner day than this one.

unread.said: You can't go that way.
You strike out to the south, and the shore there is further than it looked, and the cold is in your arms already; you turn back before it is too late, and the south shore keeps.
unread.line: You strike out to the south, and the shore there is further than it looked, and the cold is in your arms already; you turn back before it is too late, and the south shore keeps.

unread.said: You strike out to the west, and the far shore is lost in the mist and the cold is in your arms already; you turn back before it is too late, and the western shore keeps.
unread.line: You strike out to the west, and the far shore is lost in the mist and the cold is in your arms already; you turn back before it is too late, and the western shore keeps.
